predicted: SECOND ATTEMPT. The first Freddie Mac carving test (FM* jobs, 2,500 rec/site) was INCONCLUSIVE for a diagnosable reason recorded before this rerun: it was run in the wrong adequacy regime. Median EPV was 3.04 against ACS's 16.4, so every site sat far below the boundary and merging helped 63% of decisions regardless of carving -- there was no marginal decision left for carving to tip. Freddie Mac's 3% default rate means 2,500 records buys only ~75 events across 16 features. The five partitions spanned 0.00114 against a seed-to-seed sd of 0.00187, a spread/noise ratio of 0.61, and sellername sat below the geographic mean in only 2 of 3 draws (paired t p=0.448). Ordering matched the prediction; magnitude did not exist. This rerun caps at 8,250 records/site, chosen as 16*d/prevalence so median EPV lands near ACS's 16.4, and at 19 sites, the most sellername can supply at that size. NEW AND BINDING CONDITION, because the first version was mis-specified -- it tested RANK, and a five-way ordering puts sellername last 20% of the time by chance: the spread across the five partitions must exceed the seed-to-seed sd, i.e. spread/noise > 1, AND sellername must be below the geographic mean in all three draws. If either fails the economic/geographic pattern does not replicate on an independent population and comes OUT of section 11, and section 5's carving claim is scoped to collections whose sites sit near the adequacy boundary.
